approvalNote: Approved 2026-07-27, all 44 questions, for the Linear Equations end-to-end milestone.
correctionNote: Stage 4's learning-objectives note originally claimed all 8 objectives were exercised by Exercise 2.1/2.2 — that was wrong (both exercises are purely 'solve and check' procedural items; nothing there tests objectives 1-3). le-q23 through le-q28 close that gap.
expansionNote: Expansion pass (approved after Stage 6 review) added le-q23 through le-q44 — 22 new questions — to reach ~44 total, covering conceptual recognition (obj 1-3), solution verification (obj 4), error analysis, and word/application problems (numbers, ages, perimeter, currency notes, consecutive integers), none of which exist in the NCERT source. All new numbers are original, not duplicated from Exercise 2.1/2.2 or from each other. 'objective' field references the 8 objectives in stage4-learning-objectives.md by number; objective 8 (check by substitution) is satisfied by every question's expectedAnswer including an explicit check, so it is not tagged per-question separately.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: 3x = 2x + 18
hints: Transpose the 2x term to the left side of the equation.
Simplify the left side, then x is already isolated.

misconception.why: Forgetting to change the sign of 2x when moving it across the equals sign — treating transposition as a plain copy instead of a sign flip.
misconception.remediationHint: When a term crosses the equals sign, its sign flips: +2x on the right becomes -2x on the left.

questions.prompt: Solve for t and check your result: 5t - 3 = 3t - 5
hints: Transpose the 3t term to the left and the -3 to the right.
Combine like terms on each side before dividing.

misconception.why: Sign error when transposing -3, or mixing up which side the negative lands on.
misconception.remediationHint: Transpose one term at a time and re-check the sign each time before combining.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: 5x + 9 = 5 + 3x
hints: Transpose 3x to the left and 9 to the right.
2x = -4, so divide both sides by 2.

misconception.why: Dropping the negative sign when dividing -4 by 2.
misconception.remediationHint: A negative divided by a positive stays negative — recheck the sign of the final division.

questions.prompt: Solve for z and check your result: 4z + 3 = 6 + 2z
hints: Transpose 2z to the left and 3 to the right.
2z = 3, so z = 3/2 — it's fine for the solution to be a fraction.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: z = 1 (rounding, assuming a whole-number answer)
misconception.why: Students sometimes assume equations 'should' have whole-number solutions and round 3/2 down.
misconception.remediationHint: Not every equation has a whole-number solution — leave the answer as the exact fraction unless told to round.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: 2x - 1 = 14 - x
questions.expectedAnswer: x = 5. Check: LHS = 2(5) - 1 = 9, RHS = 14 - 5 = 9. LHS = RHS.
hints: Transpose -x to the left (it becomes +x) and -1 to the right (it becomes +1).
3x = 15, so divide both sides by 3.

misconception.why: Forgetting to divide by 3 after combining terms.
misconception.remediationHint: Isolating the variable means the coefficient must become 1 — always divide both sides by whatever number multiplies x.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: 8x + 4 = 3(x - 1) + 7
hints: Expand the bracket on the right first: 3(x - 1) = 3x - 3.
Simplify the right side to 3x + 4, then transpose.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: x = -8/5 (from mis-expanding 3(x-1) as 3x - 1)
misconception.why: Distributing the 3 only over the x and forgetting to multiply it by the -1 inside the bracket.
misconception.remediationHint: The number outside a bracket multiplies every term inside it, not just the first one.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: x = (4/5)(x + 10)
hints: Multiply both sides by 5 first to clear the fraction: 5x = 4(x + 10).
Expand the right side, then transpose the x terms.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: x = 8 (multiplying only the x inside the bracket by 4/5, ignoring the +10)
misconception.why: Applying the fraction to part of the bracket instead of the whole expression.
misconception.remediationHint: (4/5)(x + 10) means multiply the entire bracket by 4/5, not just the x term.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: (2x/3) + 1 = (7x/15) + 3
hints: Multiply every term by 15, the LCM of 3 and 15, to clear both fractions at once.
After clearing fractions you get 10x + 15 = 7x + 45 — transpose from there.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Multiplying only one fraction by 15 and leaving the other as-is.
misconception.why: Forgetting that every term — including whole-number terms — must be multiplied by the LCM.
misconception.remediationHint: When clearing denominators, multiply every term on both sides by the LCM, including terms that aren't fractions.

questions.prompt: Solve for y and check your result: 2y + 5/3 = 26/3 - y
hints: Multiply both sides by 3 to clear the denominators: 6y + 5 = 26 - 3y.
Transpose -3y to the left and 5 to the right, then divide.

misconception.why: Forgetting to multiply the -y term by 3 as well, leaving an inconsistent equation after clearing denominators.
misconception.remediationHint: Every term on both sides gets multiplied by the LCM — including any term that's already a whole variable.

questions.prompt: Solve for m and check your result: 3m = 5m - 8/5
hints: Transpose 5m to the left side: 3m - 5m = -8/5.
-2m = -8/5 — divide both sides by -2, keeping track of the sign.

misconception.why: Dividing -8/5 by -2 and losing track of the sign.
misconception.remediationHint: A negative divided by a negative is positive — double-check the sign when both sides of a division are negative.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: x/2 - 1/5 = x/3 + 1/4
hints: Find the LCM of all four denominators (2, 5, 3, 4) — it's 60. Multiply every term by 60.
After clearing fractions: 30x - 12 = 20x + 15. Transpose from there.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Using an incorrect common denominator, leading to a wrong equation after clearing fractions.
misconception.why: Rushing to a 'common enough' denominator instead of the true LCM of all four numbers.
misconception.remediationHint: List the prime factors of each denominator to find the true LCM before clearing fractions.

questions.prompt: Solve for n and check your result: n/2 - 3n/4 + 5n/6 = 21
hints: Multiply every term by 12, the LCM of 2, 4 and 6.
After clearing fractions: 6n - 9n + 10n = 252, which simplifies to 7n = 252.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Losing the negative sign on 9n while combining three like terms, getting 25n instead of 7n.
misconception.why: Sign errors when combining three like terms in a row.
misconception.remediationHint: Combine like terms two at a time: 6n - 9n = -3n first, then -3n + 10n = 7n.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: x + 7 - 8x/3 = 17/6 - 5x/2
hints: Multiply every term by 6, the LCM of 3, 6 and 2.
After clearing fractions: 6x + 42 - 16x = 17 - 15x. Combine like terms on the left first.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Forgetting to multiply the whole-number term (7) by 6 along with the fractional terms.
misconception.why: Treating '7' as not needing the LCM multiplier since it isn't a fraction.
misconception.remediationHint: Every term is multiplied by the LCM, whole numbers included.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: (x-5)/3 = (x-3)/5
hints: Cross-multiply: 5(x - 5) = 3(x - 3).
Expand both sides, then transpose the x terms to one side.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: x = 1 (treating it as x-5=x-3 without cross-multiplying)
misconception.why: Ignoring the different denominators and assuming the numerators can be compared directly.
misconception.remediationHint: When two fractions are equal, cross-multiply first — you can't compare numerators unless the denominators already match.

questions.prompt: Solve for t and check your result: (3t-2)/4 - (2t+3)/3 = 2/3 - t
hints: Multiply every term by 12, the LCM of 4 and 3.
After clearing fractions: 3(3t-2) - 4(2t+3) = 8 - 12t. Expand both brackets carefully, watching the signs.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Expanding -4(2t+3) as -8t + 12 instead of -8t - 12.
misconception.why: Forgetting a negative multiplier flips the sign of every term inside the bracket.
misconception.remediationHint: Distribute the negative sign into both terms of the bracket: -4(2t+3) = -8t - 12.

questions.prompt: Solve for m and check your result: m - (m-1)/2 = 1 - (m-2)/3
hints: Multiply every term by 6, the LCM of 2 and 3.
After clearing fractions: 6m - 3(m-1) = 6 - 2(m-2). Expand both brackets before transposing.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Losing track of which terms already had a denominator cleared and which didn't.
misconception.why: Applying the LCM multiplier inconsistently across terms.
misconception.remediationHint: Multiply the LCM into every single term separately, one at a time.

questions.prompt: Simplify and solve for t: 3(t - 3) = 5(2t + 1)
hints: Expand both brackets first: 3t - 9 = 10t + 5.
Transpose 10t to the left and -9 to the right.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: t = 2 (sign error transposing -9)
misconception.why: Losing the negative sign of the constant term when transposing.
misconception.remediationHint: Track the sign of every term as it crosses the equals sign.

questions.prompt: Simplify and solve for y: 15(y - 4) - 2(y - 9) + 5(y + 6) = 0
hints: Expand all three brackets first, watching the sign in front of each: -2(y-9) = -2y + 18, not -2y - 18.
Combine all the y-terms and all the constant terms separately, then solve.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Expanding -2(y - 9) as -2y - 18 instead of -2y + 18.
misconception.why: Treating the sign in front of the bracket as if it only applied to the first term inside.
misconception.remediationHint: The number in front of a bracket multiplies every term inside, including the sign: -2 × (-9) = +18.

questions.prompt: Simplify and solve for z: 3(5z - 7) - 2(9z - 11) = 4(8z - 13) - 17
hints: Expand all three brackets, being careful with the -2(9z - 11) term.
Combine like terms on each side fully before transposing anything.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Combining terms across sides before fully expanding.
misconception.why: Rushing to transpose before every bracket on both sides has been fully expanded and combined.
misconception.remediationHint: Fully expand and simplify each side of the equation independently first.

questions.prompt: Simplify and solve for f: 0.25(4f - 3) = 0.05(10f - 9)
hints: Multiply both sides by 100 to remove the decimals entirely: 25(4f-3) = 5(10f-9).
Expand both brackets, then transpose to solve for f.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Multiplying by the wrong power of 10 since 0.25 and 0.05 have different decimal places.
misconception.why: Not recognizing that clearing decimals requires the same power of 10 applied to every term on both sides.
misconception.remediationHint: Find the smallest power of 10 that turns every decimal into a whole number, then apply it to every term on both sides.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a linear equation in one variable? (a) x² + 3 = 7  (b) 2x + 5 = 11  (c) xy + 1 = 0
questions.expectedAnswer: (b) 2x + 5 = 11. It has exactly one variable and the highest power of that variable is 1. (a) is not linear because x has power 2. (c) is not linear in one variable because it has two variables, x and y.
hints: Check each option for how many variables it has, and the highest power any variable is raised to.
A linear equation in one variable has exactly one variable, and its highest power must be exactly 1.

misconception.why: Focusing only on 'it has one variable' and missing that the power must also be 1.
misconception.remediationHint: Two conditions must both hold: only one variable, AND its highest power is 1.

questions.prompt: In the equation 5x - 2 = 3x + 8, identify the LHS and the RHS.
questions.expectedAnswer: LHS (Left Hand Side) = 5x - 2. RHS (Right Hand Side) = 3x + 8.
hints: LHS means the expression written to the left of the equals sign.
RHS means the expression written to the right of the equals sign.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Naming only the variable term (e.g. LHS = 5x) instead of the whole expression on that side.
misconception.why: Confusing 'the side of the equation' with 'the term with the variable in it.'
misconception.remediationHint: LHS/RHS refers to the entire expression on each side of the equals sign, not just one term within it.

questions.prompt: State whether each of the following is an expression or an equation: (a) 5x - 2  (b) 5x - 2 = 13
questions.expectedAnswer: (a) 5x - 2 is an expression (no equality sign). (b) 5x - 2 = 13 is an equation (it has an equality sign).
hints: An equation always contains an equality (=) sign; an expression never does.
Check each item for the presence of an '=' sign.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Calling both an equation because both contain a variable and numbers.
misconception.why: Focusing on the presence of a variable rather than the defining feature — the equality sign.
misconception.remediationHint: It's the '=' sign that makes something an equation, not just having a variable in it.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are linear equations in one variable? (a) 7 = 2x - 3  (b) x + y = 10  (c) x³ - 1 = 0
questions.expectedAnswer: Only (a) 7 = 2x - 3 is a linear equation in one variable. (b) has two variables (x and y). (c) has only one variable but its highest power is 3.
hints: Check how many different variables appear in each equation.
Then check the highest power of the variable in the ones with only one variable.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Selecting (b) as well, since it 'looks like' a simple equation.
misconception.why: Not checking the variable count before checking the power.
misconception.remediationHint: Always count how many distinct letters (variables) appear before checking the power.

questions.prompt: Identify the LHS and RHS of the equation 9 - 2x = 5x + 2.
hints: LHS is everything written before the equals sign.
RHS is everything written after the equals sign.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: LHS = -2x, RHS = 5x (naming only the variable terms).
misconception.why: Treating LHS/RHS as 'the variable part' instead of the entire expression on that side.
misconception.remediationHint: LHS and RHS refer to the complete expression on each side, including every term.

questions.prompt: Translate 'thrice a number increased by 5 equals 26' into an equation, then state its LHS and RHS.
hints: Let the unknown number be x. 'Thrice a number' means 3x; 'increased by 5' means add 5.
Write the full equation first, then split it at the equals sign to get LHS and RHS.

misconception.why: Misreading the order of operations implied by the sentence — 'thrice a number' applies to the number alone.
misconception.remediationHint: Translate phrase by phrase: 'a number' = x, 'thrice a number' = 3x, then 'increased by 5' = 3x + 5.

questions.prompt: Is x = 3 a solution of the equation 4x - 5 = 7?
questions.expectedAnswer: Yes. LHS = 4(3) - 5 = 7 = RHS, so x = 3 is a solution.
hints: Substitute x = 3 into the LHS and simplify.
Compare the simplified LHS with the RHS.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: No (miscalculating 4(3) - 5 as 8 instead of 7).
misconception.why: Arithmetic slip multiplying or subtracting.
misconception.remediationHint: Work the substitution one operation at a time: 4×3=12, then 12-5=7.

questions.prompt: Is y = -2 a solution of the equation 3y + 8 = 2?
questions.expectedAnswer: Yes. LHS = 3(-2) + 8 = -6 + 8 = 2 = RHS, so y = -2 is a solution.
hints: Substitute y = -2 into the LHS, being careful with the negative sign.
Compare the result with the RHS.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: No (computing 3(-2) as +6 instead of -6).
misconception.why: Sign error multiplying a positive coefficient by a negative substituted value.
misconception.remediationHint: A positive number times a negative number is always negative: 3 × (-2) = -6.

questions.prompt: A student solved 2x + 3 = 15 and got x = 5. Check this solution. If it is wrong, find the correct value of x.
questions.expectedAnswer: The student's answer is wrong. Checking x = 5: LHS = 2(5) + 3 = 13, RHS = 15 — they don't match. Correct solution: 2x = 15 - 3 = 12, so x = 6. Check: LHS = 2(6) + 3 = 15 = RHS.
hints: Substitute the student's answer, x = 5, into the original equation and see if both sides match.
If they don't match, redo the solving steps yourself: transpose 3, then divide.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Accepting x = 5 without checking it against the original equation.
misconception.why: Skipping the verification step and trusting a plausible-looking answer.
misconception.remediationHint: Always substitute a solution back into the original equation before accepting it.

questions.prompt: A student solved 5(x - 2) = 3x + 4 as follows: 'Step 1: 5x - 2 = 3x + 4. Step 2: 2x = 6. Step 3: x = 3.' Identify the student's mistake, and find the correct solution.
questions.expectedAnswer: The mistake is in Step 1: the student expanded 5(x - 2) as 5x - 2, but it should be 5x - 10. Correct solution: 5x - 10 = 3x + 4, so 2x = 14, x = 7. Check: LHS = 5(7-2) = 25, RHS = 3(7) + 4 = 25.
hints: Check Step 1 carefully — did the student multiply the 5 by both terms inside the bracket?
Redo the bracket expansion correctly, then transpose and solve again.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Accepting x = 3 as correct because the algebra 'looks' clean.
misconception.why: Not checking each step of someone else's work against the distributive property.
misconception.remediationHint: When expanding a(b - c), the multiplier a must be applied to both b and -c.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: 6x - 7 = 3x + 11
hints: Transpose 3x to the left side.
Then transpose -7 to the right side and simplify.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Combining the constant and variable transpositions in one rushed step and mis-adding 7 and 11.
misconception.why: Rushing the transposition of two terms at once instead of one at a time.
misconception.remediationHint: Transpose one term at a time — first move the variable term, then the constant.

questions.prompt: Solve for y and check your result: 9y + 2 = 5y + 22
hints: Transpose 5y to the left side.
Then transpose 2 to the right side and simplify.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: y = 6 (arithmetic slip computing 22 - 2)
misconception.why: Simple subtraction error when isolating the constant.
misconception.remediationHint: Double-check basic subtraction/addition after transposing.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: (3x/4) - 2 = (x/2) + 3
hints: Multiply every term by 4, the LCM of the denominators 4 and 2.
After clearing fractions: 3x - 8 = 2x + 12. Transpose from there.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Forgetting to multiply the whole-number terms (-2 and +3) by 4 along with the fractions.
misconception.why: Assuming only the fractional terms need the LCM multiplier.
misconception.remediationHint: Multiply every single term on both sides by the LCM, not just the ones that started as fractions.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: 4(x - 2) = 2(x + 6)
hints: Expand both brackets first.
Then transpose the variable terms to one side and the constants to the other.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Expanding 2(x + 6) as 2x + 6 instead of 2x + 12.
misconception.why: Multiplying only the first term inside the bracket by 2.
misconception.remediationHint: The multiplier outside a bracket applies to every term inside it.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: (2x+5)/3 - (x-1)/6 = 3
hints: Multiply every term by 6, the LCM of 3 and 6.
After clearing fractions: 2(2x+5) - (x-1) = 18. Expand carefully, watching the sign in front of the second bracket.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Expanding -(x-1) as -x - 1 instead of -x + 1.
misconception.why: Forgetting that subtracting a bracket flips the sign of every term inside it.
misconception.remediationHint: Subtracting a bracket is the same as multiplying it by -1 — distribute the negative sign to every term inside.

questions.prompt: Solve for x and check your result: 0.5(3x - 4) = 0.25(2x + 10) + 1
hints: Multiply every term by 4 (or 100, then simplify) to clear the decimals.
Expand both brackets before transposing.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Multiplying only the decimal coefficients by 100 and not the '+1' term.
misconception.why: Forgetting that every term on both sides must be scaled by the same multiplier.
misconception.remediationHint: When clearing decimals, multiply every single term on both sides by the same factor, including plain numbers.

questions.prompt: A number is 5 more than another number, and their sum is 37. Find the two numbers.
questions.expectedAnswer: The numbers are 16 and 21. (x + (x+5) = 37 → 2x = 32 → x = 16, and x+5 = 21.)
hints: Let the smaller number be x, so the larger number is x + 5.
Write their sum as an equation: x + (x + 5) = 37, then solve for x.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: 16 and 22
misconception.why: Finding x = 16 correctly but then miscalculating x + 5.
misconception.remediationHint: Once you find x, substitute it back into both expressions (x and x+5) and check they actually sum to 37.

questions.prompt: Five times a number, decreased by 4, gives 26. Find the number.
hints: Let the number be x. 'Five times a number decreased by 4' means 5x - 4.
Set 5x - 4 equal to 26 and solve.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Writing 5(x - 4) = 26 instead of 5x - 4 = 26.
misconception.why: Misreading 'five times a number, decreased by 4' as 'five times (a number decreased by 4).'
misconception.remediationHint: 'Five times a number' is computed first (5x); 'decreased by 4' is then subtracted from that result.

questions.prompt: The sum of three consecutive integers is 51. Find the integers.
hints: Let the smallest integer be x. The next two are x+1 and x+2.
Add all three expressions and set the sum equal to 51.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Using x, x+2, x+4 instead of x, x+1, x+2.
misconception.why: Confusing 'consecutive integers' (differ by 1) with consecutive even or odd numbers (differ by 2).
misconception.remediationHint: Consecutive integers differ by exactly 1 each.

questions.prompt: The perimeter of a rectangle is 40 cm. Its length is 4 cm more than its breadth. Find the length and breadth.
hints: Let the breadth be x, so the length is x + 4. Recall perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth).
Set up 2(x + 4 + x) = 40 and solve for x.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Using perimeter = length + breadth (forgetting the factor of 2).
misconception.why: Misremembering the perimeter formula as simply length + breadth.
misconception.remediationHint: A rectangle has two lengths and two breadths — perimeter = 2 × (length + breadth).

questions.prompt: Raju's father is 4 times as old as Raju. Five years from now, the father will be 3 times as old as Raju will be then. Find their present ages.
questions.expectedAnswer: Raju is 10 years old and his father is 40. (4x+5 = 3(x+5) → x = 10.) Check: in 5 years Raju is 15, father is 45 = 3×15.
hints: Let Raju's present age be x, so his father's present age is 4x.
In 5 years, Raju will be x+5 and his father will be 4x+5 — set up the '3 times as old' relationship using these.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Solving 4x = 3x + 5 (applying the 'in 5 years' comparison to their present ages instead of their future ages).
misconception.why: Losing track of which point in time each part of the sentence refers to.
misconception.remediationHint: 'Five years from now' means both ages in the equation must have +5 added, not just one.

questions.prompt: A total of 25 currency notes, consisting of ₹10 and ₹20 notes, amount to ₹380. How many of each note are there?
hints: Let the number of ₹10 notes be x, so the number of ₹20 notes is (25 - x).
Write the total value as an equation: 10x + 20(25 - x) = 380.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Writing the equation as 10x + 20x = 380.
misconception.why: Not expressing the second note count as (25 - x) in terms of x.
misconception.remediationHint: Since there are only two types of notes totalling 25, the second type's count must be written as (25 - x).

questions.prompt: One-fourth of a number is 3 more than one-sixth of the same number. Find the number.
hints: Let the number be x. Translate: x/4 = x/6 + 3.
Multiply every term by 12 (the LCM of 4 and 6) to clear the fractions.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Writing the equation backwards as x/6 = x/4 + 3.
misconception.why: Misreading which fraction is described as '3 more than' the other.
misconception.remediationHint: 'A is 3 more than B' translates to A = B + 3, not B = A + 3.

questions.prompt: The width of a rectangle is two-thirds its length. If the perimeter is 60 cm, find the length and width.
hints: Let the length be x, so the width is (2/3)x. Recall perimeter = 2 × (length + width).
Set up 2(x + (2/3)x) = 60 and solve for x.

misconception.commonWrongAnswer: Treating 'width is two-thirds its length' as 'length is two-thirds its width'.
misconception.why: Losing track of which quantity the fraction applies to when translating the sentence.
misconception.remediationHint: The quantity right after 'is [fraction] its' is the one expressed in terms of the other — here, width = (2/3) × length.
